thread:
Alix Ng: :rotating_light: P1 pager — Opal (enterprise tenant, VPC in us-west-2) reporting sustained 5xx spikes and tail latency at 95th > 2.5s. Customer impact: API timeouts for 30% of requests. Root of origin unknown, likely regional capacity contention.

incident-bot: Incident created · severity=P1 · runbook=https://redwood/intra/runbooks/tenant-failures · pager=oncall@redwood.dev

Rachel SRE: I'm on this. Alix, you got a quick summary of symptoms?

Alix Ng: 5xx mainly from /v1/generate and /v1/chat streams. Error logs show OOM eglib spikes on dedicated pool nodes and some connection resets. Latency correlated with queueing on pool-usw2-dedicated-opal.

Javier Infra: I'm tailing the nodes now. CPU/GPU utilization at 98% on pool-usw2-dedicated-opal. Autoscale didn't launch warm instances — looks like quota limit on the account.

Maya AM: I’ve pinged the Opal TAM and legal/ops; they're already seeing errors. They're asking for mitigation and ETA on failover.

Sam Platform: We should failover traffic to the warm standby in us-west-1 or shift to shared-hosted fallback. Options: (A) Regional failover to us-west-1 warm pool (owned by Opal) via internal routing, (B) DNS cutover to fallback endpoints (longer TTL pain), (C) Immediate traffic split to hosted-compatible variant (model-quantized) in us-west-2.

Rachel SRE: Priorities: customer continuity, preserve tokens/data in VPC. DNS cutover is risky for VPC/private endpoints. We should prefer routing layer if available. Javier — can routing support a weighted shift at tenant granularity?

Javier Infra: Yes — rtr (internal router) supports tenant-level traffic policies. We can `rtr apply` a 100->0 shift or gradual 10% steps. There's a warm standby pool in us-west-1 (pool-usw1-opal-warm) currently at 40% capacity. I'll prepare the policy.

Alix Ng: Also confirm warm pool has compatible model version and KV caches. If not, warm-up will add latency.

Javier Infra: Model version match: yes (v2.3). KV cache empty — we can seed prefix caches using replay for hot prompt sets. I can kick that after shift.

Rachel SRE: Plan: 1) Lower DNS TTL for opal internal endpoint to 30s (precaution), 2) Gradual traffic shift via rtr 10% -> 100% to pool-usw1-opal-warm over 15m, 3) Monitor 5xx and latency, 4) If failover fails, fallback to hosted-quantized with data egress controls.

Alix Ng: Sounds good. Maya — we need to notify Opal of the plan and expected user-visible impact window (15-30m).

Maya AM: Notifying now. Draft: "We're initiating a controlled traffic shift to a warm standby in us-west-1 to restore service; short degradation possible during cutover. We'll provide updates every 10 minutes." Sending to TAM + ops.

Rachel SRE: Executing step 1: lowering TTL on internal Route53 record for opal-internal.redwood -> 30s. Javier/Tel to confirm change.

Javier Infra: Route53 change submitted:

```json
{ "ChangeBatch": { "Changes": [{ "Action": "UPSERT", "ResourceRecordSet": { "Name": "opal-internal.redwood", "Type": "A", "TTL": 30, "ResourceRecords": [{"Value":"10.10.10.5"}] } }] } }
```

Javier Infra: TTL change propagated to internal DNS — verified TTL=30 via dig on jump host.

Rachel SRE: Kicking off controlled shift: running `rtr shift --tenant opal --from pool-usw2-dedicated-opal --to pool-usw1-opal-warm --percent 10 --duration 5m --drain 2m`

incident-bot: Change recorded by Javier Infra · command=rtr shift · id=chg-2026-03-15-01

Alix Ng: Monitoring metrics: 10% started. Early indicators: 5xx count down 5% in us-west-2, slight latency increase in us-west-1 as caches cold.

Rachel SRE: Advance to 50% now. `rtr shift --tenant opal --percent 50 --duration 6m`

Javier Infra: Done. Also kicked a background prefix cache seeder: `cache-seed --tenant opal --pool pool-usw1-opal-warm --prompts /shared/opal-hot-prompts.json`

Alix Ng: Customer comms updated: notified TAM and ops that we're at 50% traffic shift, expected full cutover in ~10m.

Maya AM: Opal says they see errors reducing but still present for heavy streams. They're asking about connection affinity/keepalives.

Rachel SRE: We're seeing some failed streaming handshakes due to drained connections; those should reconnect to new pool within 30s. Lowering idle timeouts on proxies helps — Javier can we set tcp keepalive shorter?

Javier Infra: Adjusted proxy keepalive to 15s on pool-usw1 and pool-usw2. Applied via `ansible playbook: playbooks/proxy/keepalive.yml`

Alix Ng: Advancing to 100% now. `rtr shift --tenant opal --percent 100 --duration 5m`

incident-bot: Change recorded by Rachel SRE · command=rtr shift · id=chg-2026-03-15-02

Alix Ng: 100% completed. Metrics: 5xx back to baseline for Opal (within SLO). Latency at 95th still slightly higher (+300ms) but acceptable.

Maya AM: Opal confirmed primary endpoints healthy; some clients reported short reconnects but overall service restored. They asked to keep momentum until caches are warmed for next 24h.

Rachel SRE: Post-mitigation tasks: 1) Keep warm pool at +20% headroom for 4h, 2) Run health checks and synthetics against common prompts, 3) Review autoscale quota that failed earlier, file ticket to cloud quota team.

Sam Platform: Filed ticket to quota team: CLOUD-7892. Also created a rollback plan doc in the runbook: if metrics regress, `rtr revert --id chg-2026-03-15-02` will re-route back.

Alix Ng: Handoff: I'm handing to Rachel for monitoring and RCA. Rachel, take primary until 0600 UTC.

Rachel SRE: Taking over. I'll run through logs and open an RCA. Initial blameless notes: autoscale gating + capacity frag causing spike.

Maya AM: I'm drafting a post-incident update for Opal with timeline and mitigation details. Will attach logs once RCA done.

Javier Infra: Followups I'll do: 1) fix autoscale policy, 2) validate quota / request increase, 3) add alert for warm pool headroom < 30%.

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> mitigation successful. Severity downgraded to P2 for follow-ups.

Rachel SRE: Closing out here. We'll open an RCA ticket and ping the on-call SRE loop when ready. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
